domain_label: Multi-Agent Aggregation, Debate, Ensembling & Summarization (llm_engineering subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is aggregation of specialist LLM outputs including voting, weighting, debate, blending, and context compression
orchestration operates over fine-tuned specialist models; base model training is out of scope
value-weighted aggregation and summarizer-model requirement are first-class design constraints
exclusions: specialist model fine-tuning internals (covered by ftune__sft_peft)
distillation of aggregated outputs (covered by distill__kb_distill)

competency_questions.question: What aggregation strategy (vote, weighted blend, debate, cascade) is used and why was it selected over alternatives?
What is the end-to-end latency and cost model for the aggregation pipeline and how is the SLA enforced?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LATENCY_COST + AGG_ARCH + DOMAIN_ROUTER define cost/latency model

competency_questions.question: How are agent weights derived and what data is required to validate them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEIGHT_ASSIGN defines derivation and validation data requirements

competency_questions.question: How is the output distribution of the ensemble calibrated and how is calibration quality measured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CALIB_AGG + ENSEMBLE_BLEND define calibration method and ECE measurement

competency_questions.question: What is the optimal K for self-consistency and how is it selected given cost and accuracy constraints?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SC_THRESH + VOTE_SC define K selection procedure

competency_questions.question: How does multi-agent debate prevent sycophantic convergence and context overflow?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEBATE_PROTO + SUMM_COMPRESS define anti-sycophancy and budget controls

competency_questions.question: How is the judge model selected and what biases must be audited before production use?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JUDGE_MODEL defines selection and bias audit procedure

competency_questions.question: How does the summarizer/compressor node ensure key facts are retained under aggressive compression?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUMM_COMPRESS + NENKOVA_SUMM define retention metrics and thresholds

competency_questions.question: What summarization quality metrics are applied to the compressor node output and what are the acceptance thresholds?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NENKOVA_SUMM defines ROUGE/Pyramid/factual-consistency metrics and thresholds

competency_questions.question: How are post-aggregation safety violations detected and what is the escalation path?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAFETY_FILTER + HUMAN_ESCALATION define detection and escalation

competency_questions.question: How are aggregation outcomes attributed to specific agents and fed back to improve the system?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROV_TRACE + FEEDBACK_LOOP define attribution and update mechanism

competency_questions.question: How does the system guard against Goodhart's Law when optimizing aggregation on benchmark metrics?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOODHART_GUARD + EVAL_AGGR define canary metrics and benchmark rotation policy

glossary.definition: Wang et al. 2022 technique: sample K reasoning paths, select answer with highest marginal probability across paths
Du et al. 2023 technique: N model instances exchange and revise answers over R rounds before final aggregation
Jiang et al. 2023 framework: rank and blend LLM outputs using pairwise comparisons (PairRanker) and generative fusion (GenFuser)
A dedicated model or module that compresses N agent outputs to a bounded length before passing to aggregator or next debate round
Combining agent outputs using a normalized weight vector where weights reflect per-agent reliability, calibration, or value-importance
When a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure; optimizing aggregation on a fixed benchmark causes production quality divergence
Tendency of LLM judges to prefer answers in a specific position (e.g., position 1) independent of content quality
Failure mode in debate where agents converge to agreement prematurely due to social conformity pressure, not actual reasoning
Infrastructure pattern that stops routing queries to a failing agent after a threshold of failures, preventing cascade failure
Nenkova & McKeown summarization evaluation: annotate content units with importance weights; score summaries by weighted coverage

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for multi-agent aggregation, debate, ensembling, and summarization work units in absence of supplied datasets
Du et al. 2023 — Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
Wang et al. 2022 — Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
Jiang et al. 2023 — LLM-Blender: Ensembling Large Language Models with Pairwise Ranking and Generative Fusion
Nenkova & McKeown — Automatic Summarization (survey and Pyramid method)
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval, 2011

nodes.definition: Define the end-to-end architectural blueprint for combining outputs from N specialist LLM agents: choose aggregation strategy (vote, weight, cascade, debate), data-flow topology, inter-agent message schema, and latency/cost budget constraints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: N of agents or modality mix changes

pros.claim: Forces explicit cost/latency budget early, preventing runaway orchestration spend
pros.example: Latency budget set upfront avoids discovering O(N) API costs at integration

cons.claim: Wrong topology choice (cascade vs parallel) locks in latency trade-offs hard to reverse
cons.example: Cascade chosen for simplicity adds serial latency; refactor requires protocol change

failure_modes: underspecifying N-agent failure modes
ignoring context-window overflow at aggregation
no fallback for agent timeout
acceptance_tests: architecture doc reviewed and approved
latency budget traced through each hop
failure modes enumerated with fallback actions
message schema validated against all specialist output formats

nodes.definition: Assign scalar reliability weights to each specialist agent for use in weighted aggregation. Weights may derive from held-out accuracy, calibration, domain coverage scores, or value-weighted importance supplied by a domain expert.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: specialist model retrained or new eval data available

pros.claim: Value-weighted aggregation aligns agent influence with business priority
pros.example: Medical-domain agent up-weighted when patient-safety stakes are high

cons.claim: Weights derived from held-out set overfit when sets are small or domain-shifted
cons.example: 30 examples per agent insufficient for stable weight estimate

failure_modes: weights from different distribution than production
no re-weighting schedule
circular dependency: weight tuned on aggregated output
acceptance_tests: weight derivation reproducible from logged eval metrics
weight vector sums to 1 after normalization
held-out set size >= 100 examples per agent
weight sensitivity analysis documented

nodes.definition: Implement Wang et al. 2022 self-consistency: sample K reasoning paths independently from one or more models, then select the answer with the highest marginal probability (majority or plurality vote) over the answer space.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task answer space changes or K budget changes

pros.claim: Significant accuracy gain on reasoning tasks without any additional training (Wang et al. 2022)
pros.example: GSM8K CoT +17 pp with K=40 vs greedy

cons.claim: Cost scales linearly with K; for long CoT K=40 is prohibitive at inference
cons.example: K=40 * 8K tokens = 320K tokens per query

failure_modes: answer normalization misgroups equivalent answers
K too small for rare-answer tasks
dominant wrong mode in vote distribution
acceptance_tests: vote normalization tested on paraphrase equivalents
vote margin logged and thresholded
K vs accuracy curve plotted on held-out set

nodes.definition: Implement Du et al. 2023 multi-agent debate: multiple model instances independently generate candidate answers, then each reads the others' responses and revises iteratively for R rounds, with a judge or majority aggregating the final answer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: number of debate agents or rounds changes

pros.claim: Outperforms single-pass generation on factuality and math (Du et al. 2023)
pros.example: Factuality score +8 pp on biography tasks with 3 agents, 2 rounds

cons.claim: Context grows O(N*R) per round; hits context limit without compression
cons.example: 3 agents * 3 rounds * 2K tokens = 18K tokens fed back per agent per round

failure_modes: sycophantic collapse where agents agree prematurely
context overflow silently truncating prior debate
runaway rounds when no convergence criterion
acceptance_tests: convergence criterion defined and logged
context budget enforced per round
divergence detected and flagged if agents do not converge by round R

nodes.definition: Deploy a dedicated summarizer model that compresses the concatenated outputs of N specialist agents into a bounded-length context before passing to an aggregator or next debate round. Prevents context-window overflow when N*output_length exceeds the aggregator's input budget.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: N of agents changes or context-window budget revised

pros.claim: Enables arbitrarily large N without proportional context growth in downstream aggregator
pros.example: Compress 10 agent outputs from 10K to 2K tokens before final vote

cons.claim: Lossy compression risks dropping discriminative agent disagreements
cons.example: Summarizer may normalize away the specific numerical discrepancy that signals error

failure_modes: key facts silently dropped
summarizer introduces hallucinated synthesis
compression too aggressive losing answer diversity
acceptance_tests: compression tested on key-fact retention benchmark
dropped-fact log reviewed
output length <= L for all inputs
compression model evaluated separately from aggregator
revisit_triggers: key-fact retention rate drops below threshold
context window limit for aggregator changes

nodes.definition: Combine continuous (probability distribution) outputs of multiple models via weighted averaging, stacking, or mixture-of-experts gating (Jiang et al. 2023 LLM-Blender). Applies when models emit token probabilities or structured scores, not just discrete answers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model output distributions change or gating model retrained

pros.claim: Pairwise ranking (LLM-Blender) selects best outputs without access to logits
pros.example: Works on black-box API models by comparing candidate answer pairs

cons.claim: Requires logit access for probability averaging; not available from black-box APIs
cons.example: OpenAI API does not expose full token distribution

failure_modes: calibration mismatch when averaging across differently-scaled logits
gating model overfits to calibration set
stacking introduces leakage
acceptance_tests: blending evaluated vs single-best baseline
gating model validated on held-out fold
logit availability confirmed before choosing averaging method

nodes.definition: Select or fine-tune a judge LLM that evaluates and ranks candidate outputs from multiple agents, outputting a preference or score. The judge enables LLM-as-evaluator aggregation beyond majority vote when answer quality is hard to measure structurally.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: judge accuracy audit shows bias or drift

pros.claim: Enables nuanced qualitative comparison where structural metrics fail
pros.example: Open-ended generation quality: judge ranks narrative coherence when ROUGE is inadequate

cons.claim: Judges exhibit positional bias (prefer position 1) and verbosity bias (prefer longer answers)
cons.example: MT-Bench shows GPT-4 judge prefers position 1 ~60% when answers are swapped

failure_modes: judge selects its own style outputs (self-reinforcement)
judge prompt leaks evaluation criteria to generator
no audit loop to catch judge drift
acceptance_tests: positional bias measured with answer-swap test
judge agreement with human on held-out set >= 0.75
bias audit completed before production use

nodes.definition: Calibrate the aggregated output distribution so that confidence scores from the ensemble reflect true posterior probabilities. Apply temperature scaling, Platt scaling, or isotonic regression on a held-out calibration set.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: aggregation method changes or distribution shifts

pros.claim: Calibrated ensemble confidence enables principled abstention and human escalation routing
pros.example: Route to human when calibrated confidence < 0.6 threshold

cons.claim: Calibration set must match production distribution; OOD shift invalidates calibration
cons.example: Calibrated on dev set, degrades when topic distribution shifts

failure_modes: calibration set too small for isotonic regression
calibrating on same set used for weight tuning
ignoring multi-class calibration complexity
acceptance_tests: ECE post-calibration < 0.05
calibration set size >= 200
reliability diagram inspected

nodes.definition: Detect and quantify disagreement among agent outputs before aggregation. Classify conflicts as factual, structural, or uncertainty-based. High-conflict queries are flagged for human review or debate escalation rather than silent averaging.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new conflict taxonomy or escalation policy defined

pros.claim: Surfacing high-conflict cases before aggregation prevents high-confidence wrong answers
pros.example: 3 agents: 2 say answer A, 1 says B with detailed reasoning — flag for review rather than outvoting B

cons.claim: Conflict metric requires semantic comparison; lexical distance misses paraphrase agreement
cons.example: Embedding distance needed; adds latency

failure_modes: threshold too low floods human review queue
threshold too high misses real conflicts
no feedback loop from human review to threshold tuning
acceptance_tests: conflict metric validated against human-labeled disagreement set
precision/recall of escalation flag measured
threshold tuned on calibration data

nodes.definition: Enforce token budgets across all inter-agent messages, summarized contexts, and final aggregator inputs to prevent context-window overflow. Define per-agent output caps, summarizer targets, and aggregator input limits.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model context window size changes or N agents changes

pros.claim: Hard budget enforcement prevents silent truncation that corrupts aggregation
pros.example: Without cap, model silently drops earlier agents' context

cons.claim: Strict per-agent caps may force summarizer to compress high-value verbose outputs
cons.example: Medical report agent capped at 512 tokens loses key dosing detail

failure_modes: budget spec not enforced at runtime
model tokenizer mismatch causes off-by-one overflow
no alerting when budget is near-exhausted
acceptance_tests: overflow guard tested with inputs at and above limit
budget violations logged and alerted
tokenizer version pinned and verified

nodes.definition: Model and optimize the end-to-end latency and API/compute cost of the aggregation pipeline: parallel vs sequential agent calls, batching, caching, and early-exit strategies when confidence threshold is met.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pricing model changes or traffic patterns shift

pros.claim: Parallel dispatch reduces wall-clock latency from O(N) serial to O(1) amortized
pros.example: 10-agent pipeline: 10x latency reduction from serial to parallel

cons.claim: Parallel dispatch increases peak token throughput; rate limits may bottleneck
cons.example: 10 simultaneous API calls may hit token-per-minute limit

failure_modes: rate-limit errors cascade to partial aggregation
caching stale on model update
early-exit fires too aggressively missing correct minority answer
acceptance_tests: latency p95 measured under target load
cost per query tracked
early-exit accuracy parity verified

nodes.definition: Ensure that candidate outputs entering the aggregation pool are sufficiently diverse (low pairwise similarity) to benefit from ensembling. Diversity enforcement may use different temperatures, seeds, model variants, or prompt perturbations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ensemble member composition changes

pros.claim: Diverse candidates reduce bias-variance trade-off error more than correlated candidates
pros.example: Temperature 0.9 + 0.2 + prompt-perturb gives lower error than three identical T=0.7 samples

cons.claim: High temperature increases incoherence and hallucination rate in individual candidates
cons.example: T=1.2 candidates may introduce factual errors that corrupt vote

failure_modes: diverse but individually unreliable candidates degrade aggregation
diversity measured lexically not semantically
diversity enforcement conflicts with determinism requirements
acceptance_tests: mean pairwise semantic similarity measured and below threshold
individual candidate quality floor confirmed
diversity vs accuracy trade-off curve plotted
revisit_triggers: model update changes output diversity profile

nodes.definition: Define and implement the policy for escalating aggregated outputs to human review: conflict-score thresholds, confidence floor, safety-critical domain flags, and post-review feedback loop to improve agents and weights.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: domain risk profile changes or regulatory requirements updated

pros.claim: Provides a safety net for high-stakes decisions and closes the feedback loop
pros.example: Medical: escalate when <0.85 confidence; human labels feed into weight updates

cons.claim: High escalation rate overwhelms human reviewers and negates automation benefit
cons.example: 10% conflict rate at 1M qpd = 100K human reviews/day — infeasible

failure_modes: no feedback path from human review to system improvement
escalation queue not monitored
threshold set without considering reviewer capacity
acceptance_tests: escalation rate measured and within reviewer capacity
feedback loop traced from human label to next weight update
escalation latency SLA defined

nodes.definition: Define metrics and test sets for measuring aggregation quality: accuracy gain vs best single model, diversity-accuracy trade-off, judge-human agreement, calibration ECE, cost-per-correct-answer, and latency percentiles.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: production metrics diverge from offline eval

pros.claim: Multi-metric eval prevents Goodhart: optimizing one metric (accuracy) while cost explodes
pros.example: Track cost-per-correct alongside accuracy to prevent K=40 vote overkill

cons.claim: Comprehensive eval suite is expensive to maintain when aggregation architecture changes
cons.example: Each architecture change invalidates baselines requiring re-run

failure_modes: eval set contaminated with training data
offline eval metrics not predictive of production
no baseline comparison to single-model
acceptance_tests: eval suite covers all primary metrics
baseline single-model result documented
eval set contamination check passed
regression on known-good configuration verified

nodes.definition: Detect and mitigate Goodhart's Law in aggregation tuning: weights, K, or judge prompts optimized to a fixed benchmark overfit the benchmark while failing on production. Includes held-out test set discipline, canary metrics, and periodic benchmark rotation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark performance diverges from canary metrics

pros.claim: Canary metrics catch Goodhart before production degradation
pros.example: Internal canary shows 5 pp drop when benchmark shows continued improvement

cons.claim: Benchmark rotation requires significant re-annotation cost and slows tuning cycles
cons.example: New benchmark every quarter requires 500-hour annotation effort

failure_modes: no separation between tune set and test set
benchmark leaked into summarizer training
weight optimization loop directly on test set
acceptance_tests: test set not used in weight/K tuning loop
canary metric correlation with production measured
contamination scan completed before each release
revisit_triggers: benchmark score rises while canary stagnates
new LLM training data includes known benchmarks

nodes.definition: Monitor the live aggregation pipeline for agent failures, timeout spikes, token-budget violations, cost anomalies, conflict rate changes, and output quality drift. Includes alerting, circuit-breaker logic for failing agents, and automatic fallback to reduced-agent subset.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new agent type or infrastructure change

pros.claim: Circuit breaker prevents cascading failure when one specialist agent degrades
pros.example: Agent A timeout: circuit opens, fallback to 3-agent subset, quality degrades gracefully

cons.claim: Monitoring adds per-query overhead and requires careful metric selection to avoid alert fatigue
cons.example: Too many metrics → noisy alerts → SREs ignore them

failure_modes: no fallback when circuit opens
alert thresholds not tuned causing false positives
monitoring data not fed back into evaluation
acceptance_tests: circuit breaker tested with injected agent failure
fallback quality measured
alert thresholds validated on historical data

nodes.definition: Implement the loop that collects production outcomes (human labels, downstream task success, user ratings), attributes them to aggregation decisions, and propagates improvements back to weight updates, K selection, and judge prompt refinement.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: production outcome metrics change or label collection policy changes

pros.claim: Closes the loop so aggregation quality improves over time rather than stagnating post-launch
pros.example: Monthly weight refresh from production labels improved accuracy 3 pp over static ensemble

cons.claim: Attribution of production outcomes to specific aggregation decisions is hard with joint inference
cons.example: Outcome depends on agent A+B+judge jointly; isolating which component improved is difficult

failure_modes: attribution error leads to wrong component being updated
feedback loop latency too long to catch fast distribution shifts
no version control on weight/K changes
acceptance_tests: attribution methodology documented and validated
feedback latency <= defined threshold
version control on all updated parameters confirmed

nodes.definition: Route incoming queries to the appropriate subset of specialist agents based on query domain, intent, or confidence. Prevents irrelevant agents from adding noise to aggregation and reduces cost by activating only relevant specialists.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new domain or specialist agent added

pros.claim: Reduces cost and latency by only calling relevant specialists
pros.example: Medical query: activate medical+pharmacology agents only, skip creative-writing agent

cons.claim: Routing errors exclude the correct specialist, causing systematic blind spots
cons.example: Ambiguous query mislabeled as 'finance' misses the 'legal' agent that has the answer

failure_modes: routing model trained on different distribution than production
no fallback when confidence is low
new domain not covered by routing taxonomy
acceptance_tests: routing accuracy >= 0.90 on held-out query set
fallback to full pool tested
taxonomy coverage documented for all deployed agents

nodes.definition: Apply a safety/policy filter on aggregated outputs before delivery: detect harmful, biased, or policy-violating content in the ensemble output, block or rephrase, and log for audit. Distinct from per-agent filtering; catches emergent harms from combination.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: policy guidelines update or new harm category identified

pros.claim: Catches emergent harmful combinations that pass per-agent filters individually
pros.example: Agent A says X; agent B says Y; combined output implies harmful Z that neither alone would produce

cons.claim: Post-aggregation filter adds latency and may block legitimate outputs due to false positives
cons.example: Conservative filter blocks 2% of valid medical answers causing user harm

failure_modes: filter optimized for single-agent outputs misses ensemble-specific harms
no audit log making post-hoc review impossible
filter not updated when policy changes
acceptance_tests: filter tested on adversarial prompt set
false positive rate measured
audit log retention confirmed
policy change workflow documented

nodes.definition: Determine the optimal number of samples K and confidence threshold for self-consistency vote, balancing accuracy gains against cost. Includes K vs accuracy curve analysis, budget-constrained K selection, and early-exit threshold when vote margin exceeds target.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cost budget changes or accuracy target revised

pros.claim: K-accuracy curve often plateaus; operating on plateau saves cost without accuracy loss
pros.example: K=20 reaches 98% of K=40 accuracy at half the cost on GSM8K-style tasks

cons.claim: Optimal K varies by task difficulty; single K setting sub-optimal across query mix
cons.example: K=10 sufficient for easy queries wastes budget on hard ones

failure_modes: K selected on easy set underperforms on hard production queries
early-exit fires before plateau in vote margin
no periodic re-evaluation of K as model updates
acceptance_tests: K-accuracy curve documented
early-exit accuracy parity confirmed
cost at chosen K within budget

nodes.definition: Record which agents contributed to each aggregated output, their individual answers, weights applied, and the aggregation decision path. Enables debugging, auditing, and attribution of errors to specific components.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: audit requirements change or new agent added

pros.claim: Enables post-hoc debugging: trace exactly which agent produced the wrong answer in a failed aggregation
pros.example: Find that agent B's wrong answer was up-weighted due to stale weight vector

cons.claim: Full provenance logging increases storage cost proportional to N agents and query volume
cons.example: 10 agents * 2K tokens each * 1M qpd = 20B tokens/day of logs

failure_modes: logging overhead causes latency spike
logs not indexed making retrieval slow
no log retention policy causing compliance risk
acceptance_tests: provenance records retrievable within SLA
storage cost estimated and budgeted
log retention policy compliant with data regulations

nodes.definition: Apply Nenkova & McKeown automatic summarization evaluation framework: ROUGE, Pyramid method, and content unit coverage to assess the quality of the summarizer/compressor node outputs. Ensures the compressor node retains high-value content units.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: summarizer model updated or task type changes

pros.claim: Pyramid method captures content unit importance beyond surface n-gram overlap (Nenkova & McKeown)
pros.example: Identifies that ROUGE misses dropped key facts that Pyramid captures

cons.claim: ROUGE correlates poorly with factual correctness in LLM-generated summaries
cons.example: High ROUGE-2 summary drops a numerical fact with no penalty

failure_modes: using ROUGE as sole quality metric for factual summaries
reference summaries not updated when agent outputs change
no factual consistency check
acceptance_tests: ROUGE and Pyramid scores above threshold
factual consistency scorer applied
reference set reviewed periodically

Blending uses per-agent weights from weight assignment

Diversity enforcement ensures vote pool has sufficient variation
Summarizer enables debate by bounding per-round context
Summarizer is primary mechanism for meeting context budget
Summarization quality metrics evaluate compressor output
Debate transcript provides per-agent divergence signal for conflict scoring
Conflict score is primary routing input for human escalation
Calibrated confidence provides second routing signal for escalation
Calibration applied to blended distribution output

edges.resolution_rule: enforce held-out test discipline: weight optimization must not touch the Goodhart guard test set; rotate canary metrics quarterly

edges.rationale: Debate adds O(N*R) API calls conflicting with latency/cost SLA
edges.resolution_rule: cap rounds R at budget; use summarizer between rounds; activate debate only for high-conflict queries above conflict threshold

edges.rationale: Aggressive summarization may drop discriminative agent disagreements needed for debate
edges.resolution_rule: measure key-fact retention on debate-relevant facts specifically; set minimum compression fidelity threshold before debate uses summarized context

edges.rationale: High diversity changes output distribution, invalidating calibration from low-diversity regime
edges.resolution_rule: calibrate on diverse-candidate distribution specifically; do not reuse calibration set from low-diversity regime

edges.rationale: Synchronous human escalation conflicts with latency SLA
edges.resolution_rule: async escalation queue: do not block synchronous response on human review; return provisional answer with uncertainty flag

edges.rationale: Production outcome labels trigger weight updates
Production cost-accuracy data drives K schedule updates
Runtime monitoring triggers feedback loop on quality drift
Monitor alerts can trigger manual escalation when automated escalation fails
Provenance records enable accurate outcome attribution in feedback loop
Provenance enables per-agent contribution analysis in evaluation
Domain routing determines which weight vector applies to the active agent subset
Routing to fewer agents directly reduces per-query cost and latency
Safety filter false positive rate is a tracked metric in evaluation framework
Goodhart guard enforces eval discipline that underpins evaluation framework validity
Context budget specification constrains summarizer target length (non-dependency: parallel design concerns)
Summarization quality metrics are a sub-component of overall evaluation framework

conflict_axes.name: Aggregation Quality vs Latency/Cost
conflict_axes.description: Adding more agents, more debate rounds, or higher K improves quality but compounds API cost and latency O(N*R*K).
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use parallel dispatch, early-exit, domain routing, and K-accuracy plateau to operate on the Pareto frontier.

conflict_axes.name: Summarizer Compression vs Information Retention
conflict_axes.description: More aggressive compression reduces context cost but risks losing discriminative agent disagreements or key facts.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Set minimum key-fact retention threshold; audit dropped-fact log; prefer extractive compression for high-stakes facts.

conflict_axes.name: Diversity vs Individual Reliability
conflict_axes.description: High diversity in the candidate pool improves ensemble value but increases individual hallucination rate.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Set quality floor on individual candidates before admitting to pool; measure diversity vs accuracy jointly.

conflict_axes.name: Benchmark Optimization vs Production Validity (Goodhart)
conflict_axes.description: Optimizing weights/K on a fixed benchmark causes Goodhart overfitting, improving benchmark score while production quality stagnates.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Strict train/test separation; rotate canary metrics; never tune weights on the held-out test set.

conflict_axes.name: Human Escalation Thoroughness vs Automation Scalability
conflict_axes.description: Aggressive escalation to human review ensures safety but overwhelms reviewers and breaks automation SLAs.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use async escalation queue; calibrate escalation threshold to reviewer capacity; prioritize by risk tier.

conflict_axes.name: Debate Context Growth vs Context Budget
conflict_axes.description: Multi-round debate generates context that grows O(N*R), overflowing aggregator context window without summarizer intervention.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Summarize between rounds; enforce hard per-round context cap; limit R by budget not by convergence alone.

conflict_axes.name: Judge Model Self-Reinforcement vs Objectivity
conflict_axes.description: A judge model may prefer outputs similar to its own style, creating a feedback loop that biases aggregation toward one model family.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use judge from different model family than generators; audit positional bias; diversify judges over time.

conflict_axes.name: Provenance Logging Cost vs Observability
conflict_axes.description: Full provenance logging enables debugging but adds storage cost proportional to N agents and query volume.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Sample-based provenance logging at configurable rate; full logging only for flagged or high-conflict queries.

conflict_axes.name: Safety Filter False Positives vs Coverage
conflict_axes.description: Conservative post-aggregation safety filter blocks harmful combinations but increases false positive rate on legitimate outputs.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Measure false positive rate; tune threshold per domain risk tier; route FP-blocked outputs to human review rather than hard reject.

conflict_axes.name: Weight Stability vs Adaptability
conflict_axes.description: Frequent weight updates improve tracking of distribution shifts but introduce instability and complicate provenance.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Version-control all weight changes; gate updates behind eval regression suite; enforce minimum update interval.

edge_cases.scenario: All N agents produce identical wrong answers
edge_cases.mitigation: Conflict detection cannot detect correlated failures; require diverse model families; use canary test set to detect systematic error
edge_cases.detection_signal: canary metric drop without conflict signal

edge_cases.scenario: Summarizer hallucinates synthesis not present in any agent output
edge_cases.mitigation: Factual consistency check on summarizer output against source; flag novel claims; prefer extractive over abstractive for factual content

edge_cases.scenario: Context budget exceeded at runtime when N agents produce unexpectedly long outputs
edge_cases.mitigation: Hard token cap enforced at agent output collection; overflow triggers summarizer even if not in normal path

edge_cases.scenario: Debate agents reach sycophantic consensus on wrong answer within 1 round
edge_cases.mitigation: Require minimum divergence at round 1; if consensus too fast, inject adversarial prompt to stress-test agreement
edge_cases.detection_signal: round-1 convergence with low initial diversity

edge_cases.scenario: Weight vector stale after specialist model retrained
edge_cases.mitigation: Model version change triggers mandatory weight re-derivation; version-lock weight vector to model version

edge_cases.scenario: Domain router mislabels query as wrong domain, excluding correct specialist
edge_cases.mitigation: Low-confidence routing falls back to full agent pool; routing confidence logged for audit

edge_cases.scenario: Safety filter false-positive blocks time-critical medical query
edge_cases.mitigation: Domain-specific safety thresholds; medical queries route to human review on block rather than hard reject with delay
edge_cases.detection_signal: safety block rate spike in medical domain

edge_cases.scenario: Production benchmark contamination: aggregation weights tuned on leaked test set
edge_cases.mitigation: Contamination scan before each weight tuning run; canary metrics independent of tuning set

edge_cases.scenario: Orchestration pipeline partial failure: 3 of 10 agents timeout, aggregation proceeds on 7
edge_cases.mitigation: Circuit breaker opens failed agent; weight vector renormalized over available agents; quality degradation logged

edge_cases.scenario: Feedback attribution error: wrong agent credited for production success, inflating its weight
edge_cases.mitigation: Require provenance record for every feedback event; periodic offline attribution audit
edge_cases.detection_signal: offline audit shows weight-outcome correlation mismatch

edge_cases.scenario: Self-consistency vote margin ties at K/2 each for two answers
edge_cases.mitigation: Tie-breaking by judge model; log tie events; increment K if tie rate exceeds threshold

edge_cases.scenario: Aggregated output inherits combined bias from multiple biased agents amplified by weighting
edge_cases.mitigation: Bias audit on aggregated output distribution separately from per-agent audit; monitor demographic disparity in outputs

dominance_rules.rule: AGG_ARCH must be finalized before any aggregation sub-component is implemented
dominance_rules.rationale: Architecture decisions (topology, context limit, strategy) cascade to all downstream components; rework cost is O(N) without upfront design
dominance_rules.applies_when: any sub-component (VOTE_SC, DEBATE_PROTO, WEIGHT_ASSIGN) is being designed

dominance_rules.rule: SUMM_COMPRESS must be validated on key-fact retention BEFORE being used in DEBATE_PROTO
dominance_rules.rationale: Lossy summarization in the debate context degrades the quality of subsequent debate rounds irreversibly without notice
dominance_rules.applies_when: debate mode activated with N agents

dominance_rules.rule: GOODHART_GUARD discipline overrides any weight or K optimization showing benchmark improvement
dominance_rules.rationale: Benchmark improvement without canary corroboration indicates overfitting; production quality is the true objective
dominance_rules.applies_when: weight or K update shows benchmark gain without canary gain

dominance_rules.rule: SAFETY_FILTER must be applied to aggregated output before delivery regardless of aggregation method
dominance_rules.rationale: Emergent harmful combinations from multi-agent outputs bypass per-agent filters; post-aggregation filter is non-optional

dominance_rules.rule: CONTEXT_BUDGET hard limits must be enforced before calling aggregator model
dominance_rules.rationale: Silent truncation by the aggregator corrupts aggregation more than explicit budget enforcement causing graceful degradation

dominance_rules.rule: WEIGHT_ASSIGN must be version-locked to specialist model version
dominance_rules.rationale: Weights derived from model version V are invalid for model version V+1; stale weights silently miscalibrate aggregation
dominance_rules.applies_when: any specialist model is updated or replaced

dominance_rules.rule: CONFLICT_DETECT must run before HUMAN_ESCALATION to provide routing signal
dominance_rules.rationale: Escalation without conflict score cannot distinguish high-risk from routine outputs; conflict score is the primary routing feature

dominance_rules.rule: DIVERSITY_ENFORCE must confirm minimum diversity before self-consistency voting
dominance_rules.rationale: Low-diversity candidate pool degrades ensemble to near single-model performance; diversity check is a prerequisite gate

dominance_rules.rule: PROV_TRACE must be active before FEEDBACK_LOOP to ensure attribution integrity
dominance_rules.rationale: Feedback without provenance leads to attribution errors that corrupt weight updates and amplify errors over time

dominance_rules.rule: DOMAIN_ROUTER fallback to full agent pool must activate when routing confidence is below threshold
dominance_rules.rationale: Overconfident routing that excludes correct specialist is worse than running all agents at higher cost

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not implement aggregation method before architecture is locked
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Full re-implementation of aggregation logic when topology or context limit changes
anti_rework_rules.check: AGG_ARCH lifecycle_state == locked before starting VOTE_SC or DEBATE_PROTO implementation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not derive agent weights before held-out eval set is confirmed sufficient (>= 100 per agent)
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Unreliable weights require full re-derivation when larger eval set is obtained
anti_rework_rules.check: WEIGHT_ASSIGN acceptance test: held-out set size verified before weight computation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not tune K or debate rounds on the Goodhart guard test set
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Test set contamination requires building a new held-out benchmark, losing comparability
anti_rework_rules.check: GOODHART_GUARD: confirm K/R tuning used only on dev/calibration split

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy summarizer without measuring key-fact retention
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Lossy summarizer corrupts debate and aggregation, requiring summarizer replacement and re-evaluation
anti_rework_rules.check: SUMM_COMPRESS: key-fact retention metric computed and above threshold before integration

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not calibrate ensemble before aggregation method is finalized
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Calibration is invalidated if blending method or weight vector changes, requiring full recalibration
anti_rework_rules.check: CALIB_AGG: aggregation method and weights confirmed stable before calibration run

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not enable feedback loop before provenance tracing is active
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Attribution errors silently corrupt weight updates, requiring manual audit and rollback
anti_rework_rules.check: PROV_TRACE confirmed active; FEEDBACK_LOOP has attribution validation test

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not expand N agents without updating context budget and summarizer target
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Context overflow corrupts aggregation; summarizer undertargets compression causing downstream failures
anti_rework_rules.check: CONTEXT_BUDGET updated when N increases; SUMM_COMPRESS re-evaluated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not lock judge model choice without completing positional bias audit
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Positional bias systematically favors agent outputs in position 1, biasing aggregation permanently
anti_rework_rules.check: JUDGE_MODEL: answer-swap test completed; bias audit documented before deployment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change aggregator model without re-running calibration
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Calibration from old model distribution is invalid, causing overconfident routing and human escalation errors
anti_rework_rules.check: CALIB_AGG: re-run triggered on model version change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not assume per-agent safety filters catch all post-aggregation harms
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Emergent harmful combinations bypass per-agent filters; safety incidents require emergency patch and audit
anti_rework_rules.check: SAFETY_FILTER adversarial test set specifically targeting ensemble-level harms

iteration_protocol.trigger: N of agents changes by more than 2
iteration_protocol.action: Revisit AGG_ARCH, CONTEXT_BUDGET, SUMM_COMPRESS target length, WEIGHT_ASSIGN, and ORCH_MONITOR thresholds
Trigger WEIGHT_ASSIGN re-derivation, CALIB_AGG recalibration, DIVERSITY_ENFORCE re-measurement; version-lock weight vector to new model version

iteration_protocol.trigger: Production accuracy degrades > threshold vs offline eval
iteration_protocol.action: Run GOODHART_GUARD contamination scan; audit PROV_TRACE for attribution errors; re-evaluate WEIGHT_ASSIGN on fresh held-out data

iteration_protocol.trigger: Conflict detection false negative rate exceeds 10%
iteration_protocol.action: Recalibrate CONFLICT_DETECT threshold; review conflict taxonomy; update HUMAN_ESCALATION routing policy

iteration_protocol.trigger: Summarizer key-fact retention drops below threshold
iteration_protocol.action: Re-evaluate SUMM_COMPRESS model and compression ratio; reduce target compression; review NENKOVA_SUMM metrics
Review LATENCY_COST model; enable parallel dispatch if not active; review DOMAIN_ROUTER to reduce active agents; adjust SC_THRESH K downward
Audit JUDGE_MODEL for new bias types; run answer-swap test; consider rotating to different judge model family

iteration_protocol.trigger: Safety filter false positive rate exceeds threshold
iteration_protocol.action: Review SAFETY_FILTER thresholds per domain; expand domain-specific safe phrase list; route FP-blocked queries to HUMAN_ESCALATION

iteration_protocol.trigger: Domain shift detected in production query distribution
iteration_protocol.action: Update DOMAIN_ROUTER taxonomy; re-derive WEIGHT_ASSIGN on new distribution sample; audit GOODHART_GUARD for benchmark validity

iteration_protocol.trigger: Feedback loop latency exceeds defined threshold
iteration_protocol.action: Review FEEDBACK_LOOP attribution pipeline; increase label collection frequency; audit PROV_TRACE storage performance

priority_rationale.AGG_ARCH: Foundation: all other components depend on architectural decisions
priority_rationale.CONTEXT_BUDGET: Hard constraint: overflow corrupts all downstream aggregation
priority_rationale.SUMM_COMPRESS: Enables N-agent scale without context blowup; required by debate and budget
priority_rationale.WEIGHT_ASSIGN: Determines quality of weighted aggregation; high risk if stale
priority_rationale.DOMAIN_ROUTER: Reduces cost/latency and focuses aggregation on relevant agents
priority_rationale.SAFETY_FILTER: Non-optional for production; emergent harms not caught by per-agent filters
priority_rationale.HUMAN_ESCALATION: Risk mitigation: high-conflict and safety-critical path must be defined early
priority_rationale.CONFLICT_DETECT: Gate for human escalation; needed before escalation policy is active
priority_rationale.DEBATE_PROTO: High-value but high-cost; requires summarizer and budget management
priority_rationale.VOTE_SC: Core aggregation method; well-understood and robust
priority_rationale.ENSEMBLE_BLEND: Advanced blending; requires logit access and calibration
priority_rationale.JUDGE_MODEL: Needed for nuanced quality eval; bias audit gating before production
priority_rationale.SC_THRESH: Optimization of vote; lower priority than vote implementation
priority_rationale.DIVERSITY_ENFORCE: Prerequisite for vote quality; but can be added after initial deployment
priority_rationale.CALIB_AGG: Important for escalation routing; requires stable aggregation first
priority_rationale.EVAL_AGGR: Evaluation framework; needed to validate all other components
priority_rationale.FEEDBACK_LOOP: Continuous improvement; requires provenance and monitoring first
priority_rationale.PROV_TRACE: Audit/debug enabler; required for feedback loop integrity
priority_rationale.NENKOVA_SUMM: Evaluates summarizer; important but downstream of summarizer deployment
